entries.title: Monomial invariant slope with arbitrary invariant intercept theorem
entries.scope: Let A=k[u,v,x,y] over a characteristic-zero field, D=u*partial_x+v*partial_y, B=ker(D)=k[u,v,u*y-v*x], and q=u^r*v^s*x+b with r>=1, s>=0, and arbitrary b in B. Then D(q*A) is Mathieu-Zhao. For b nonzero, writing delta=q-b in B_(uv)[q], the lowest-u face moment argument forces f to have positive u-order; when s>=1, the independent lowest-v face forces positive v-order. Thus eventual pure-power membership puts f in u*B[q] for s=0 and in u*v*B[q] for s>=1, which clears every fixed mixed-primitive denominator. For b=0, D(q*A)=u^r*v^s*D(x*A); divisibility supplies the required u and v content, while the moving-linear theorem supplies the B[x] normal form and accepts the fixed multiplier denominator. This is an internal proof, depends on the one-variable polynomial moment lemma, and has not been externally reviewed.

entries.title: Complete coprime invariant-slope theorem
entries.scope: Let A=k[u,v,x,y], D=u*partial_x+v*partial_y, B=ker(D)=k[u,v,w], and q=a*x+b for arbitrary nonzero coprime a,b in B. Then D(q*A) is Mathieu-Zhao. For each irreducible factor pi of a other than u, the lowest pi-face of the zero-constant primitive is divisible by q-b; coprimality makes the endpoint b mod pi nonzero, and the one-variable moment lemma forces positive pi-order of every eventual-power seed. The u-face gives the same conclusion when u divides a. When u does not divide a, its face root is beta=(b mod u)-(a mod u)*w/v. If beta is nonzero, the moment lemma forces positive u-order. If beta is zero, the equality v*(b mod u)=(a mod u)*w is equivalent to q lying in u*A; then D(q*A) is contained in u*A, so eventual pure membership directly forces u to divide the seed. In every case the accumulated radical content clears u*a and every fixed mixed denominator. Only a nontrivial common invariant factor of a,b remains outside this theorem. This is an internal proof and has not been externally reviewed.
supersedes_notes: all coprime nonmonomial invariant slopes, including aligned conductor descent, as live counterexample charts

entries.title: Complete invariant-linear principal-carrier theorem
entries.scope: Let A=k[u,v,x,y], D=u*partial_x+v*partial_y, B=ker(D)=k[u,v,w], and q=a*x+b for arbitrary a,b in B with a nonzero. Then D(q*A) is Mathieu-Zhao, without a coprimality assumption. The abstract scaling lemma says that if M is a Mathieu-Zhao subspace of a domain and c*M is contained in M, then c*M is Mathieu-Zhao: from eventual f^m in c*M, choose one large N and apply the Mathieu property of M to the fixed multiplier g*f^N/c. Writing c=gcd(a,b) and q=c*q_0, LND-GCS or the moving-linear theorem makes M=D(q_0*A) Mathieu-Zhao. Since c is invariant, D(q*A)=c*M and M is a B-module, so the scaling lemma applies. This closes every degree-one carrier already presented in the generic B[x] slice. LND-IAC supplies the intrinsic denominator descent and multiplicity step for all remaining one-root principal carriers. This is an internal proof and has not been externally reviewed.

entries.title: Invariant-affine carrier and thickening theorem
entries.scope: Let A=k[u,v,x,y], D=u*partial_x+v*partial_y, and B=ker(D)=k[u,v,w]. If H is a noninvariant irreducible polynomial with D^2(H)=0, then D(H*A) is Mathieu-Zhao. Writing s=D(H)=b_1*u+b_2*v gives H=b_0+b_1*x+b_2*y and embeds A in B_s[H]. At each irreducible pi dividing s, one of u,v is a unit in B_(pi), and the corresponding inverse coordinate is unit*(H-beta_tilde)/s. Every negative pi-face is therefore divisible by H-beta. The endpoint beta cannot vanish, because the inverse identities would imply H in pi*A, contradicting irreducibility and noninvariance. Eventual pure powers and the one-variable polynomial moment lemma force positive pi-order at every denominator prime, which clears the primitive of every fixed mixed multiple. If h lies in ker(D^2) minus ker(D), then h=c*H with c in B and one such H; divisibility bootstrapping proves D(H^d*A) Mathieu-Zhao for every d>=1, and the Mathieu scaling lemma restores c^d. The checker replays the invariant-affine coordinate identities but not the all-order moment argument. This is an internal proof and has not been externally reviewed.

entries.title: Complete principal-ideal theorem for the rank-two linear model LND
entries.scope: Let A=k[u,v,x,y] over a characteristic-zero field and D=u*partial_x+v*partial_y. Then D(q*A) is Mathieu-Zhao for every nonzero q in A. If q is invariant, this follows from the plinth-power theorem for D(A) and Mathieu scaling. Otherwise view q over Frac(ker(D)) in the generic orbit coordinate. Two or more distinct roots give zero eventual-power radical by LND-GTR. With one root, UFD factorization and A_u=B_u[x] show that q=c*H^d with c invariant and H the unique noninvariant irreducible factor of generic degree one; equivalently D^2(H)=0. LND-IAC handles H^d and scaling removes c. This closes all principal ideals only for this model derivation. Genuinely nonprincipal ideals outside the existing finite-residual and plinth-power theorems, and general locally nilpotent derivations not reducible to this two-slice normal form, remain open. The proof is internal, unformalized, and has not been externally reviewed.

entries.title: All-dimensional singular-gradient stratum and DVR-torsion law
entries.scope: Let grad(Psi):A^n->A^n have degree m>=2, let its top potential depend on r<n essential variables, and let C be an irreducible component of dimension s and degree d in the projective singular locus of the essential top hypersurface. The corresponding reduced infinity component is Join(P^(n-r-1),C), of dimension n-r+s, codimension r-s in P^n, and degree d. At its generic point let B_C be the transverse top Jacobian algebra of length mu_C. The active lower-layer gradient quotient is a finite module over R=K[[epsilon]] and therefore has a unique DVR profile R^rho direct-sum_j R/(epsilon^a_j), with rho plus the number of torsion summands equal to mu_C. After adjoining epsilon^m its exact active length is L_C=m*rho+sum_j min(m,a_j). Quotienting by the epsilon-divisible missing kernel gradients leaves a final transverse length lambda_C satisfying mu_C<=lambda_C<=L_C<=m*mu_C, and the component contributes d*lambda_C to sigma_(r-s). If rho=0 and every torsion order is one, or if a missing component is epsilon times a unit, the contribution is exactly d*mu_C. If the active module is flat, a missing initial form epsilon^q*s gives the sharper upper bound d*(m*mu_C-(m-q)*dim(B_C*s)). Without flatness, the torsion orders are essential. The repeated-root binary quintic h5=x^3*y^2 has mu_C=2, while h4=0, x*y^3, and y^4 give active profiles of truncated lengths 8, 3, and 2 for m=4, proving that singular-locus dimension, Hessian rank, and transverse top multiplicity do not determine the Segre contribution. HC4PPG9 applies the order-one active law to binary root partitions. The theorem does not compute the DVR profile for the remaining HC4 singular packets or determine later Segre components.

entries.title: Six-variable quartic HN Waring-rank rigidity through rank nine
entries.scope: Over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, no essential six-variable homogeneous quartic Hessian-nilpotent polynomial has Waring rank at most eight. At rank nine, every essential quartic HN polynomial has polynomially invertible gradient map z -> z-grad(P). Consequently every essential six-variable quartic HN counterexample has Waring rank at least ten. In rank ten, the HN trace identities exclude every projective Gale parallel class of multiplicity at least four and every pair of distinct triple classes. Thus every remaining rank-ten candidate has parallel-class multiplicity at most two except possibly one triple class. The finite codimension-two Gale, one-latitude rank-nine, complementary-minor, and rank-ten parallel-obstruction calculations are exact SymPy checks; the coordinate-free trace, matroid base-packing, Hesse, and Witt-index arguments are written proofs. QHNW1 does not prove the residual cyclic-complement matroid lemma or a rank-eleven lower bound, and it has not received external mathematical review.

entries.title: Rank-ten Gale-matroid survivors and the nonsimple trace obstruction
entries.scope: The cyclic-complement lemma formerly proposed in OP-QHNW10 is false: U_(4,6) direct-sum U_(0,4) is a literal characteristic-zero counterexample, and duplicating the first three columns of the displayed seven-point family K_simp(a,b), with realization scheme Spec Q[a,b,1/(ab(a-1)(b-1))], gives a loopless rational counterexample. The literal loop survivor cannot support a rank-six Gram matrix satisfying the first two HN traces because its four free Waring covectors would span a totally isotropic four-plane. Relative to the rank-four catalogues through nine simple points distributed by matroid-database 0.3, the complete loopless nonsimple slice has 37 coloured survivor types over 17 simplifications. Two normalized realization ideals are the unit ideal over Q and the remaining 35 types have rational points. Every one of those 35 types contains a six-element rank-two Gale flat. On its four-dimensional kernel the first trace forces the six Gram diagonal entries to vanish, the second trace forces the whole Gram block to vanish, and the six-dimensional Witt bound excludes every rank-six Gram matrix on the type. The checked-in script freezes and replays the returned catalogue records but does not regenerate the external catalogue. This result does not enumerate simple rank-four matroids on ten elements, construct a rank-ten HN counterexample, or raise the Waring lower bound to eleven, and it has not received external mathematical review.

entries.title: Binary root-partition Segre sieve
entries.scope: Let psi=q2+h3+h4+h5 be a collision-normalized degree-five HC4 candidate whose top quintic has essential Hessian rank two and is a singular binary form. At a root p of multiplicity e>=2, the two top partial derivatives have transverse orders e-1 and e, so the transverse Jacobian algebra is K[x]/(x^(e-1)) and has length e-1. Assume at every repeated root that, after eliminating the leading transverse active equation, one redundant active gradient component has initial form epsilon times a unit. Then the active DVR profile consists of e-1 order-one torsion summands, and PGS3 gives component contribution e-1. If the binary quintic has q distinct roots, sigma2=sum_p(e_p-1)=5-q. Essential rank two excludes the pure fifth power, leaving partitions 2+1+1+1 with sigma2=1, 3+1+1 and 2+2+1 with sigma2=2, and 4+1 and 3+2 with sigma2=3. Their affine-degree-two/three atlas intersections contain respectively 51/50, 44/43, and 37/36 rows. Thus the generic double-root packet shrinks from 260/249 codimension-two rows to 51/50 on this open lower-layer stratum. The theorem excludes no row unconditionally: failure of the active-unit condition is a proper higher-X0-torsion stratum, and its constant-Hessian determinant faces remain open.

entries.title: All-degree squarefree top-Hessian obstruction for direct HC4
entries.scope: Let Psi be a characteristic-zero four-variable polynomial of degree D>2 with constant nonzero Hessian determinant, and suppose the top homogeneous Hessian has generic rank three. Gordan--Noether gives a constant top-kernel direction and a ternary top form f. The first two scaled determinant faces force the transverse diagonal to vanish at first order and then impose q*det(Hess(f))=grad(a)^T*adj(Hess(f))*grad(a). Hence every rank-three top cone of a hypothetical HC4 counterexample has nonsquarefree ternary Hessian determinant. entries.title: Nonreduced Hessian--Schur module normalization gate
entries.scope: Continuing the nonsquarefree frontier of HC4DIR2, let C be a symmetric 3-by-3 matrix of ternary degree-r forms with nonzero determinant Delta, and let d have degree r-1 with Delta dividing d^T*adj(C)*d. The cokernel of C is self-dual with twist 2r, and the adjugate is its symmetric pairing. On every irreducible component Q where C has generic corank one, the local Smith form forces the kernel coordinate of d halfway into the nonreduced thickening. Let P be the componentwise-minimal denominator clearing C^(-1)*d, rho=deg(P), and e=P*C^(-1)*d. Then P^2 divides Delta and e has degree rho-1. On the normalization of every component Q dividing P, let K_Q be the saturated kernel line and B_Q the divisor where the induced rank-two form drops rank. One has K_Q^2=O(B_Q-2r), and the nonzero residue of e gives deg(B_Q)>=2*deg(Q)*(r+1-rho). For the ternary-quintic packet r=3, 1<=rho<=4. Hence either rho=4 and Delta=P^2*ell with ell linear, or rho<=3 and every essential denominator component carries the stated positive corank-two defect. On the rho=4 packet the Schur problem is equivalently det(C)=P^2*ell, C*e=P*d, and d^T*e=P*a for a linear form a; Hessian and gradient integrability are imposed afterward. This is a structural reduction, not an exclusion or construction of an HC4 counterexample. Generic corank-two and corank-three Smith strata, including the radial sextic calibration, remain separate.

entries.title: Exact septuple-linear Hessian--Schur exclusion
entries.scope: Continue HC4NHM1 and HC4DIR27 on the generic-corank-one ternary-quintic Schur stratum det(Hess(h5))=ell^7*R2, with R2 squarefree and coprime to ell. If ell is essential in the minimal denominator clearing C^(-1)*d, its pole order b is 1, 2, or 3. On the normalized line, the saturated kernel is O(-kappa), the corank-two defect has length 6-2*kappa, and the nonzero cleared residue forces 0<=kappa<=b-1. Hence exactly six (b,kappa,defect) rows occur: (1,0,6), (2,0,6), (2,1,4), (3,0,6), (3,1,4), and (3,2,2). On the extremal (3,2,2) row the primitive kernel is a basepoint-free triple of binary quadratics. If its image is a projective line, Hessian integrability either drops the boundary Hessian to rank at most one or forces ell to have determinant multiplicity exactly one. Thus every repeated-line survivor on this row has a nondegenerate conic kernel. In boundary jets h5=F5+ell*G4+ell^2*H3/2+ell^3*J2/6+..., writing the conic kernel as (a,b,c), one has det(Hess(F5))=lambda*a^2 and the first-normal coefficient forces a^2 to divide 2*a*(b*H_y+c*H_z)+(b,c)*Hess(G4)*(b,c)^T; when it does, J2 is unique. On repeated-root binary quintics, the square-Hessian condition leaves the partitions 4+1, 3+2, 3+1+1, and 2+2+1, together with one exceptional 2+1+1+1 orbit characterized by (t^2-t+1)^3/(t^2*(1-t)^2)=25/4. On the squarefree stratum, an exact saturated factorization elimination gives a reduced degree-twelve marked scheme; all points form one PGL2 orbit, represented by F=u^5+v^5, whose Hessian is 400*u^3*v^3. Solving the complete tangent-kernel spaces for every repeated-root type and for the Fermat orbit shows that all but the 4+1 case have a common quadratic kernel factor; the primitive 4+1 family is killed by its first-normal remainder. Hence the extremal (3,2,2) row is empty. The same moving-line-image argument applies to primitive degree-one kernels and makes both defect-four rows empty. The three remaining constant-kernel rows split into transverse and tangent directions. The transverse direction successively kills every normal jet and makes det(C)=0. In the tangent direction, exact determinant faces either make the x^7 coefficient vanish or force it to be a scalar multiple of a square linear form, contradicting the squarefree residual quadratic. Hence the complete exact-septuple generic-corank-one packet with squarefree coprime cofactor is empty. Multiplicity eight/nine are outside this theorem and are subsequently closed by HC4NHM3. The nonsquarefree residual-quadratic incidence is subsequently classified by HC4NHM4 and excluded from four-variable prolongation by HC4NHM5; lower-Smith boundaries remain open.

The first transverse normal equation D(s)=-C^2*G/3 has the polynomial solution s=-2/C-I^2*L/144 because the apparent pole cancels against a constant-ring invariant. The resulting full normal--tangent form jet is polynomial and its source-fiber vector is divergence-free. That vector is not locally nilpotent because C divides its nonzero C-component, so a single finite exponential does not give a four-dimensional polynomial normalizer. For the canonical minimal first jet, the order-F residual of the formal-flow second jet has no tangent--tangent terms and only three q-independent normal coefficients. Bezout gives a polynomial form correction Z, but fiber-volume compatibility requires D(lambda)=-div(Z). The grading wt(C)=2, wt(G)=-3, wt(W)=-6 forces lambda=G*C*p(N,J); its coefficient recurrence reaches p_5=-17/5388768 and then has a nonzero constant tail at every order. Hence the canonical minimal first jet has no polynomial volume-compatible second completion. The divergence obstruction is affine-linear in an arbitrary first-jet shift h. The grading shows that only ker(D)_{-2}=I^2*U*K[S] can change its weight-two class. For the leading monomial I^2*U*S^m, r=m+2, the top J^r coefficient of p_5 is (-1728)^r*(r-1)*(3r-4)*(3r-2)*(3r-1)*(9r^2-24r-5)/716636160, which is nonzero for every integer r>=2. Descending on deg(K) excludes every nonzero K, while K=0 leaves p_5=-17/5388768. Thus no polynomial invariant first-jet shift admits a second completion, and no polynomial R21 normalizer can have this degree-seven F as target-b component. In the full reciprocal Bezout ansatz Q_H=Q+H(G,C), the fiber bracket is {F_H,W_H}|_(F_H=0)=-H_G, so R21 compatibility forces H=G^2/2+k(C); this is only the ambient symplectic shear Q->Q+k(C), and the complete source form is unchanged. Every other Bezout pair is (R+B*T,S-A*T) and changes only the companion W->W-T*F. Hence the all-invariant second-order no-go excludes the complete compatible Bezout ansatz. More generally, for independent base translations F=-B*P+A*Q+K(G,C), W=R*P+S*Q+L(G,C), the complete source form differs from the canonical form in exactly one dG^dC coefficient, and that coefficient is the fiber-admission PDE. Every admitted affine-momentum row therefore has the same excluded full form. Abstractly, after a fiber and first-jet admission, the class [div(Z)] in A/D(A) is a well-defined second-order obstruction because all form corrections differ by lambda*D. R21 remains exactly fiber-admitted; this construction-level route did not decide global admission, which is separately obstructed by DC2HL3.

entries.title: R21 global symplectic-boundary audit and Hamiltonian Derksen gate
entries.scope: For the reciprocal R21 graph form on A4, the six coefficient degrees in the displayed (x,y,z,e) coordinates are (16,13,11,16,11,11). Its generic pole order on the coordinate P4 is nineteen, and its highest homogeneous part is the rank-two integrable form 2*x^5*y^9*z*dy wedge (3*z*dx+x*dz). These data do not descend to the Aut(A4)-orbit: for every N>=1, the elementary automorphism (a,b,c,d)->(a,b+a^N*c,c,d) pulls the standard form back to omega_std+a^N*da wedge dc, which has pole order N+3 and a decomposable leading form. The R21 Pfaffian is one, so its top volume equals the standard top volume exactly, while P*dQ+e*dR is a polynomial primitive and I=0 is not an affine pole or residue divisor. Thus raw primitive pole data, fixed-P4 contact degeneration, and crepant data from the top wedge cannot obstruct global polynomial Darboux admission. For the Danielewski constant rings R_n=K[I,S,U_n]/(I^n*U_n-S*(S-sigma)), the center (I,U_2) is a complete intersection at two reduced points and has Rees algebra R_2[X,Y]/(I*Y-U_2*X); its I-chart U_2=I*V is exactly R_3. Hence the ordinary affine modification realizes rather than obstructs the exponent-two to exponent-three crossing, and the missing datum is its symplectic normal thickening. Define HD(A,Omega)=K[f:X_f is locally nilpotent] and HML(A,Omega)=intersection_(X_f LND) ker(X_f). These are polynomial-symplectic invariants; standard Darboux admission forces HD=A and HML=K. For R21, exact inverse-Jacobian calculation gives x dividing nonzero X_P(x), x dividing nonzero X_Q(x), and (1+x*y^2) dividing nonzero X_e(1+x*y^2), so X_P,X_Q,X_e are not locally nilpotent, while X_R=partial_e is locally nilpotent. On each of K[P,R], K[Q,R], and K[e,R], the Hamiltonian-LND polynomials are exactly K[R]. Hamiltonian LNDs outside these slices are not classified, so HD properness and global R21 non-admission remain open.

entries.title: R21 target-subalgebra Hamiltonian-LND classification
entries.scope: Let Omega_21=dP wedge dQ+de wedge dR be the reciprocal R21 graph form over Q[q]/(q^2-4q+6), and define X_f by contraction of X_f with Omega_21 equal to df. For every f in K[P,Q,R], X_f is locally nilpotent if and only if f belongs to K[R]; the same equivalence holds for f in K[e,R]. Indeed X_R=partial_e, so K[R] gives LNDs. Exact inverse-Jacobian calculation gives x dividing both X_P(x) and X_Q(x), with nonzero quotients. Hence for f in K[P,Q,R], local nilpotence forces X_f(x)=0. If f_P and f_Q were not both zero, their ratio would equal -X_Q(x)/X_P(x) in K(P,Q,R). In the quartic inverse root T, specialization P=1,Q=0 gives -3*T*(2*T^3-5)/(4*(T^3-4)). The polynomial T^4-4*T+4*R is irreducible over K(R), and equality of this ratio to a base scalar c(R) leaves the nonzero remainder -4*c*T^3-9*T+24*R+16*c. Thus f_P=f_Q=0. Separately, (1+x*y^2) divides nonzero X_e(1+x*y^2), while X_R fixes 1+x*y^2, giving the K[e,R] row. This classifies only the displayed target subalgebras, not Hamiltonian LNDs in the full source ring K[x,y,z,e].

entries.title: Complete stable-independent R21 Hamiltonian-LND classification
entries.scope: For the reciprocal R21 form on A4, let C=K[x,y,z]. For every f in C, the Hamiltonian derivation X_f is locally nilpotent on C[e] if and only if f belongs to K[R]. The reverse direction is X_(h(R))=h'(R)*partial_e. For the forward direction, X_f preserves C and R. Write R=x*S with S polynomial and S at x=0 equal to one. Factorial closure of an LND kernel forces both x and S to be fixed. After extending to K(x), a nonzero LND of K(x)[y,z] would make S a polynomial in a coordinate, so generic components of S=c would normalize to affine lines. Instead S-c is quadratic in z with discriminant -x^3*(6*c*(1+x*y^2)^2-5*x*y^2-6)/18. In u=x*y^2 its branch polynomial is 6*c*u^2+(12*c-5)*u+6*(c-1), with discriminant 24*c+25 and nonzero constant term, hence four distinct geometric branch points and genus one. Thus the restricted LND is zero. Contraction then gives df=h*dR. The analogous generic-R branch polynomial 6*r*u^2+(12*r-5*x)*u+6*(r-x), with discriminant x*(24*r+25*x), proves that the generic R-fiber is geometrically integral, so K(R) is relatively algebraically closed in K(x,y,z) and f belongs to K(R). Finally R(x,0,0)=x forces a polynomial f in K(R) to lie in K[R]. Hamiltonians with positive e-degree are not classified, so the full Hamiltonian-LND generator algebra and global polynomial Darboux admission remain open.

entries.title: Global R21 Hamiltonian-LND classification and polynomial-Darboux obstruction
entries.scope: Let A=K[x,y,z,e] in characteristic zero with the reciprocal R21 form Omega_21=dP wedge dQ+de wedge dR, and define X_f by contraction with Omega_21 equal to df. Then X_f is locally nilpotent if and only if f belongs to K[R]. Indeed the stable-independent theorem DC2HL2 first proves that every LND of C=K[x,y,z] preserving R is zero and that Y_g=0 for the C-part of a Hamiltonian forces g in K[R]. For an arbitrary f=sum_(j=0)^m e^j*f_j, use the e-degree filtration. If the top C-part Y_(f_m) is nonzero, the highest homogeneous derivation e^m*Y_(f_m) is an LND of C[e], so Y_(f_m) is a forbidden nonzero LND of C fixing R. Hence f_m=h(R). The next homogeneous layer is delta=e^(m-1)*(Y_(f_(m-1))+m*h(R)*Z)+e^m*h'(R)*partial_e, where Z=X_e restricted to C and Z(R)=-1. Since e divides delta(e), the LND divisibility lemma forces h'=0. If h=c is nonzero, E=Y_(f_(m-1))+m*c*Z is an LND of C with E(R)=-m*c. Thus a scalar multiple of R is a slice, and the slice theorem makes (R) prime, contradicting the nontrivial factorization R=x*S. Therefore m=0, and DC2HL2 gives f in K[R]. Conversely X_(h(R))=h'(R)*partial_e is locally nilpotent. Consequently HD(A,Omega_21)=K[R] and HML(A,Omega_21)=K[x,y,z]. A polynomial Darboux chart would pull back the four standard coordinate Hamiltonians to locally nilpotent Hamiltonians generating A, which is impossible because every such Hamiltonian lies in K[R]. Therefore Omega_21 is not equivalent under Aut(A4) to the standard polynomial symplectic form. This settles global polynomial Darboux admission for R21, but it does not prove DC2 without the separate quantization bridge.

entries.title: R21 graph-centralizer exhaustion and strict filtered quantization no-go
entries.scope: Let C=K[x,y,z] for the reciprocal R21 Keller triple (P,Q,R), and let delta_P, delta_Q, delta_R be its commuting inverse-Jacobian derivations. In D(C)=A3, the transported graph-normal pair a'=delta_P, b'=P-delta_Q satisfies [a',b']=1. Its complete centralizer is K<R,delta_R,delta_Q,Q-delta_P>, whose displayed generators form two commuting Weyl pairs and hence a copy of A2. Exhaustion follows from the left PBW expansion: commutation with delta_P fixes every coefficient by delta_P, while commutation with P-delta_Q gives delta_Q(c_beta)=-(beta_P+1)c_(beta+e_P). The generic-R geometric-integrality theorem and R(x,0,0)=x give ker_C(delta_P) intersect ker_C(delta_Q)=K[R], so descending in beta_P integrates only powers of Q with constants in K[R], exactly the normal ordering in Q-delta_P. This centralizer is precisely the image of the corresponding target A2 centralizer under the ambient inverse-Jacobian A3 endomorphism. Therefore restriction is an isomorphism onto a transported A2, and any identification with a fixed A2 gives an automorphism rather than a non-surjective endomorphism. Separately, no filtered PBW quantization B with gr(B)=(K[x,y,z,e],Pi_21) can have a strict filtered Weyl frame: inner derivations of four Weyl generators are locally nilpotent, so their highest-symbol Hamiltonian derivations are locally nilpotent; DC2HL3 puts all four symbols in K[R], which cannot generate the associated graded algebra. Thus the natural graph-centralizer reduction and every strict filtered PBW bridge are excluded. This does not settle DC2 or rule out an essentially filtration-collapsing, non-PBW identification of a global R21 quantization with A2.

entries.scope: The nine genuine A1/MW16 hit labels in the complete 63,917-class ICARM atlas are reconstructed with exact degree-one shells and saturated determinant-474 generic MW16 bases. Thus the initial wave recovers 38 of 55 demonstrated directions, fully recovers two curves, and comes within one on three. The completed curve-398 adaptive wave adds nine directions, and a new complete curve-400 wave searches all 4*(2^5-1)=124 nonzero quotient lifts with no timeout and gives M16->M21->M28, adding seven directions. A further exact arithmetic audit computes global minimal models for all 104 fibres, explicitly transports all 1,664 generic sections, re-proves rank-16 independence by finite reduction, and records all 856 frozen pointed charts. A fixed menu of rational scalings, section-slope translations, reciprocal coordinates and three-section projective coordinates is selected only by coefficient bit sizes. No prospective candidate reaches residual 2-Selmer or expensive continuation, and Nagao-to-unrestricted-point-search remains forbidden.

entries.title: Exact false negative for incremental CRT height-beam pruning
entries.scope: For the four prime groups at 19, 23, 29, and 37 pinned in the regression, incremental width-one beam pruning selects a final rational representative of height 1409. Complete enumeration of all 160 CRT choices instead finds residue 238875 modulo 468901, with exact rational representative 48/53 of height 53 and residues 7,20,2,3. True minimum height is nondecreasing along each fixed branch because feasible sets shrink; the counterexample instead shows that relative branch ordering can change, so a finite height-scored beam can discard the best completed branch. entries.title: Finite uniform J1 bound for the two rootless determinant-948 frames
entries.scope: For every complex projective K3 surface of Picard rank 19, the rank-three transcendental Hodge-isometry group is exactly {+id,-id}: any nonreal action on H^(2,0), or an opposite sign on its real orthogonal line, would create a nonzero rational (1,1) class in the transcendental lattice. The mass-complete rootless J2 classification has exactly two realized classes, so the number of rootless Jacobian fibrations modulo surface automorphisms is at least 2 and at most 8. This is not an exact J1 classification: improving the bound with the recorded frame-automorphism images requires ample-cone stabilizer control or an equivalent surface-automorphism computation.

entries.title: Physical orbit-96 A7+D7 equation and Mordell--Weil representation 1+chi_-3+1
entries.scope: For the determinant-36 E6+A1 Picard-rank-19 K3, the orbit-96 divisor is D96=2P0+(2,1,2,2,1,0)_E6a+(1,0,0,0,0,0)_E6b+A3_2. The ordinary IV* resolution has chart order (leaf,+outer,-outer,+inner,-inner,central), coordinate valuations u=(2,1,1,2,2,3), x=(2,2,2,3,3,4), y=(3,2,2,4,4,6), and the marked P0 entrance fixes the physical root-to-chart map (2,1,4,6,5,3). These data prove that z=(t+1)*(y+y0+m_tan*(x-x0))/(x-x0)^2 has exactly the vertical pole cycles in D96, so <1,z> is the complete resolved H0 basis. Coercing m_tan back to the old-base polynomial ring and checking the quadratic discriminant against b^2-4ac gives a squarefree quartic with rational points. Its Jacobian is y^2=x^3-27*I6(z)*x-27*J9(z), with coefficient lists in the canonical note and certificate, and fibres I8 at zero, I3* at infinity, and seven I1 fibres. Thus the roots are A7+D7, Euler number 24, torsion is trivial, geometric MW rank is three, and the saturated height lattice is diag(3/8,1,3). With E6a_6 as zero, three exact section divisor classes generate this lattice. Sqrt(-3)-conjugation swaps only the old I4 side components and acts on the height basis as diag(1,-1,1). Hence the generator fields are QQ(k)(z), QQ(k,sqrt(-3))(z), QQ(k)(z), and the arithmetic rank over QQ(k)(z) is exactly two. Orbit 96 has the same chi_-3 line as orbit 103, not a complementary quadratic character. Polynomial child-coordinate formulas for all generators and ranks of numerical specializations are not claimed.

entries.title: Orbit-103 arithmetic rank two and comparison with the physical orbit-96 A7+D7 model
entries.scope: On the exact orbit-103 2D5+2A2 Weierstrass K3, the two polynomial QQ(k)(r)-sections Q+ and Q- each have P.O=0 and local corrections 5/4+2/3+2/3, hence height 17/12. They are neither equal nor negatives; trivial geometric torsion and equality of their positive heights therefore prove independence. The old-base binary quartic has leading coefficient -48*(r+k)^2/(k^2*(k^2-4)^2). Its infinity points give an explicit section Q_delta=(X_delta,sqrt(-3)*Y_delta0), with the degree-four and degree-six polynomials displayed in the canonical note. Exact substitution holds and sqrt(-3)-conjugation sends Q_delta to -Q_delta. Thus the geometric rank-three MW representation contains a nonzero anti-invariant line, while Q+ and Q- span a rank-two invariant subspace. The generic arithmetic rank over QQ(k)(r) is exactly two. The corrected physical orbit-96 certificate gives fibres I8+I3*+7I1, arithmetic rank two, and representation 1+chi_-3+1. Thus orbit 103 is source-divisor-sparser, orbit 96 is fibre-sparser and has lower displayed Weierstrass degrees, but neither supplies a third rational direction and their nontrivial quadratic characters are the same.

entries.title: Seven exact orbit-103 specializations of rank at least seven
entries.scope: For the orbit-103 E6+A1 family, a bounded two-stage local-trace search exhausts rational k of projective height at most 3000, retains eight k values, exhausts rational r of height at most 5000 for each, and separately retains the top 1000 k=1 candidates of r-height at most 500. No selected fibre has certified rank at least eight; the selected distribution is not a frequency statement for the full height box, no rank upper bound is claimed, and the proposed rank-8--12 success condition remains unmet.

entries.title: Five-edge physical corridor from the NS0031 A1+2A7 marking to F017/MW17
entries.scope: Inside the determinant-1184 NS0031 Neron--Severi lattice, exact primitive degree-two neighbours give the chain A1+2A7 -> A1+2A3+A5 -> 5A1+A3 -> 4A1 -> A1 -> rootless F017/MW17. This is a marking-level physical-connectivity theorem inside a bounded meeting search, not global route optimality or an equation-level QQ corridor.

entries.title: Degree-three and sampled degree-four low-genus cover visibility at the R17 rank-25--28 fibres
entries.scope: For the four published R17 controls, every split point in the complete 39,120-class degree-two atlas is expressed integrally in the ordered known basis, giving exact exceptional quotient ranks 5,3,2,1 at ranks 25,26,27,28. A deterministic inversion-closed 1,025-coset degree-three frontier sample contributes 69 norm-20 equation representatives, all with irreducible residual cubics; the complete deep degree-three census contributes exactly 320 norm-26 translation cosets and 160 inversion representatives, all with irreducible residual cubics and squarefree discriminant degree four. A deterministic inversion-closed 1,025-coset degree-four sample contributes 53 norm-34 equation representatives, with generic factor patterns 45 irreducible quartics and eight 2+2 decompositions. Exact factorization at all four controls finds no rational component in any of these 282 new covers, so the cumulative captured exceptional ranks remain 5,3,2,1 through degrees three and four. There are no parallel duplicate quotient classes; the sole fundamental circuit is orbit-1cb25 - orbit-0cff7 + orbit-1ea09 - orbit-0d4ca=0 at rank 25. The prioritized rank-28 fibre still exposes only Q2-Q4+Q5-Q8+Q10, at trace norm 10 and deterministic group-addition cost 11. Zero gain at the requested degree-four layer triggers the declared stop, so degrees five and six were not tested. The norm-26 shell is complete, but the 69 norm-20 and 53 norm-34 equation sets are bounded deterministic samples; the result does not exclude splitting elsewhere in the 18,024,296 norm-20 cosets or in M/4M, does not prove that the known subgroup is saturated or full, and gives no Mordell--Weil rank upper bound.

entries.title: R17 visibility-complexity baseline separates rigid and post-hoc mechanisms
entries.scope: For an atlas and cost order frozen before the target point Q and fibre t, visibility complexity is the Pareto frontier of the mechanism class, genus, multisection degree, linear-system dimension, incidence codimension, normalized branch-equation cost, and coefficient-field complexity; only rigid and genuinely predeclared-pencil witnesses are predictive. Exact certificate joins at the four published rank-25--28 R17 controls show that four of the 38 ordered displayed generators have minimum rational-curve degree two: Q1,Q3,Q5,Q6 at rank 25. The remaining 34 rational-curve degrees are UNKNOWN because only degree two is complete and the degree-three/four equation subatlases are incomplete. The familiar 5,3,2,1 values are span dimensions of split rational bisections, not counts of individually exposed named generators; those counts are 4,0,0,0. Using the common trace tau=-P2-P5, exact target-fitted line incidence gives every one of the 38 generators a genus-one degree-two witness with linear-system dimension and incidence codimension both one. These are post-hoc incidence witnesses: no leakage-free predeclaration ledger accompanies them, so predeclared trace-pencilled degree remains UNKNOWN for all 38. Primitive branch-polynomial support and coefficient-bit costs, rational pencil-parameter heights, and the earlier construction-cost tuples are recorded direction by direction. No norm-20 rational-trisection or M/4M quadrisection enumeration is performed. This proves no equality L_t=E_t(Q), no saturation or rank upper bound, no rational-curve non-existence in degrees at least three, and no monotonic visibility-complexity theorem; increasing rigid visibility complexity is a conjecture.

entries.title: Rational one-parameter E6 quadratic base change with exact rank split 2+1
entries.scope: For a rational parameter r off an explicit finite exceptional set, the rational elliptic surface y^2=x^3+a*u*x+u*(u+c), with a=2*(r^2+r+1)/(r+1) and c=-2*r^2/(r+1), has fibres IV*+II+2I1 and exact MW rank two generated by (1,u+1) and (r^2,u+r^3). The twist by d=u*(u+c) has exact rank one generated by (0,1). The quadratic pullback u=-c/(1-t^2) is a nonconstant K3 family with fibres 2IV*+IV+4I1, exact generic Picard rank 19, saturated MW rank three with invariant/anti-invariant split 2+1, trivial torsion, and abs(disc NS)=24. Blichfeldt's Hermite bound proves that the same NS cannot contain a rootless rank-17 frame, so no same-NS rootless MW17 fibration exists. No rank-sum-four family is asserted.

entries.title: Complete first quadratic-neighbour shell with six nef A6+D7 Mordell--Weil-rank-four frames
entries.scope: For the determinant-24 Picard-rank-19 E6+II quadratic-base-change K3, every zero-neutral old-degree-two class is represented in the split marking by D=2e+2f-w with w^2=8. Exact dominant-label and rank-three closest-vector enumeration gives 268 current-Weyl orbits, of which three are nonprimitive. Physical reduction leaves 211 classes at old degree two, 42 at degree one, and 12 at degree zero. The minimum child root rank is 13 and occurs in exactly six classes, all with root type A6+D7. Each has no physical fixed component, passes the complete old-section height-ellipsoid gate and the degree-two horizontal-root exclusion, and therefore defines a nef Jacobian fibration of exact geometric Mordell--Weil rank four, trivial torsion, and regulator 6/7. The q=2 shell contains no lower-root or rootless frame; independently, EC-K3-RES-QBC-E6-II-RANK3-RHO19 rules out every same-NS rootless MW17 frame. No child equation or arithmetic descent of the four geometric generators over QQ(r) is asserted.

entries.title: Rationalized D6 surface and exact obstruction in its polynomial two-section chart
entries.scope: The generic D6 rational elliptic surface is written over QQ as y^2=x^3+u^2*(-u^2+a*u-3)*x+u^3*(g*u^3+b*u^2+a*u-2), without the customary sqrt(3) normalization at infinity. A two-parameter polynomial section chart is verified by literal substitution. Equality up to sign of the leading y coefficients for two sections yields two nontrivial correspondence curves. Explicit birational maps identify both with Y^2=X^3+X^2+X, whose Mordell--Weil group over QQ has rank zero and torsion {O,(0,0)}; both torsion points are degenerate or omitted correspondence boundaries. Hence this particular polynomial marked-section chart contains no nontrivial rational pair. This does not obstruct a second section in a larger D6 rational-function chart or a rank-sum-four construction.

entries.title: Exact two-marked D5 seed and complete GF(11) polynomial two-twist census
entries.scope: The rational elliptic surface y^2=x^3+u^2*(-3*u^2-13*u-3)*x+u^3*(2*u^3-17*u^2-12*u-2) has discriminant order seven at u=0 with squarefree residual finite discriminant, and contains the sections P=(-u-2*u^2,u^2) and Q=(-u-u^2,u^2*(1-2*u)). At u=1 they specialize to a signed Mordell--Weil basis on the exact rank-two curve y^2=x^3-19*x-29, proving P,Q independent over QQ(u). Over GF(11), complete enumeration of all 110 monic squarefree quadratic twists d and all 1331 polynomial x of degree at most two tests 146410 incidences in the chart d*y^2=x^3+f*x+g with degree y at most two. Exactly one twist, d=u^2-2*u-2, has two distinct-x sections. No relation with coefficient box [-12,12]^2 is found, but that bounded check is not a height or independence certificate. No characteristic-zero lift, rational 2+2 family, or rank-sum-five construction is asserted.

entries.title: Exact D5 low-section eliminants and nonrationality of the p=11,13 lifts
entries.scope: For the two saturated seven-variable low-section systems through the regular D5 survivors, exact block Groebner elimination over QQ gives a degree-142 t-eliminant on A=-1 with irreducible factor degrees 2,2,4,4,42,88 and a degree-128 t-eliminant on A=2 with factor degrees 2,4,44,78. Neither eliminant has a linear factor over QQ, so neither complete saturated slice has a rational point. The residue t=8 mod 11 selects the irreducible degree-88 factor in the first slice, and t=2 mod 13 selects the irreducible degree-78 factor in the second; both selected roots are simple modulo their primes. Thus the two previously unique p-adic lifts are nonrational algebraic points with exact t-fields QQ[t]/(H88) and QQ[t]/(H78), whose primitive coefficient vectors are pinned. This closes only the two declared low-section slices, not the full D5 polynomial coefficient ideal or another first-section slice.

entries.title: Exact dependence or extra-fibre obstruction in the normalized two-point A4 Tate slice
entries.scope: In the normalized two-point Tate slice y^2+a1*x*y+a3*y=x^3+a2*x^2 with a1=1+A*u, h=H*u, kappa=B*u+C*u^2, a2=kappa, and a3=h*(1-h-a1)+kappa, the points P=(0,0) and Q=(h,h^2) are automatic. On B nonzero, the u^4 discriminant coefficient is -B^2*(H+B)*(A+H-B), so an I5 fibre at u=0 has branches H=-B and H=B-A. In both branches Delta/u^5 contains the square factor (B+(A*B-B^2+C)*u)^2. Avoiding the resulting extra repeated discriminant root, generically an I2 fibre, forces C=B^2-A*B; exact function-field group arithmetic then gives P+2Q=0 on H=-B and 3P+2Q=0 on H=B-A. Thus this particular pure-A4 slice cannot provide two independent marked directions. This does not obstruct a general two-point Tate chart with nonconstant Bezout data or a two-marked A4 surface outside the declared slice.

entries.title: Exact norm-eight genus-one bisection pencil through all eleven published R17 rank-28 targets
entries.scope: On the published rootless R17 elliptic K3, complete enumeration of the minimum-norm-eight shell gives 230,040 stored short representatives and exactly 63,925 translation classes. The equation-cheapest class has trace tau=-P2-P5, trace denominator degree two, and one-addition equation cost. For tau=(Nx/h^2,Ny/h^3), the unique degree-below-four M0 satisfying M0*Nx+Ny=0 modulo h^2 extends to the genus-one pencil M=M0+lambda*h^2. For each of the eleven public exceptional points at t=-9529/5471, the exact line-incidence equation gives a rational lambda. All eleven normalized branch polynomials q=(M^4-6*M^2*Nx-8*M*Ny-3*Nx^2-4*A*h^4)/h^6 are irreducible squarefree quartics over QQ, coprime to h and the degree-24 surface discriminant. Each degree-two base change has a height-16 anti-invariant section independent of invariant R17 and hence generic rank at least 18 over its genus-one base. The 11/11 incidence is the expected selection of the unique member of a genus-one pencil through each nondegenerate point; it does not discover the known points, classify all 63,925 pencils or the 43 norm-twelve deep classes, produce a rank-32 specialization, or prove simultaneous splitting away from the fitted control.

entries.title: Common rank-two integral character glue for the eleven fitted rank-28 lifts
entries.scope: Relative to the chosen norm-eight trace pencil with tau=-P2-P5, each of the eleven exact genus-one-cover lifts through the public rank-28 specialization has invariant trace tau of pulled-back height 16 and an anti-invariant difference T_i of height 16, with tau.T_i=0 and 2R_i=tau+T_i. Primitive normalization proves that the eleven irreducible squarefree quartics define eleven distinct deck-character squareclasses. This is one repeated character-saturation pattern for eleven fitted lifts, not an intrinsic invariant of an isolated fibre point, one cover carrying eleven anti-invariant directions, a root-annihilating bridge reglue, a new specialization, or a rank-32 result.

entries.title: E6 rational unordered quotient and genus-one ordered rank-four incidence
entries.scope: In the full split marked E6 chart y^2=x^3+(a*u-3)*x+(u^2+c*u-2), coefficient elimination for two complete node-collision linear-chord pencils with common squareclass u*(u-M) gives unordered incidence components of geometric genera zero and two. The genus-zero quotient has the smooth rational point (S,M)=(2,16) and the exact parameterization S=-(k^2+1)(k^4+2k^2+13)/(4k(k^2+3)), M=-2(k^2+1)(k^2+3)/k^3. Recovering P=vw shows S^2-4P is a rational square times k^4+6k^2+13. Hence the ordered data v,w,ell_v,ell_w live on the genus-one cover r^2=k^4+6k^2+13, birational to Cremona 52a2: Y^2=X^3-64X-192. A proved rank calculation gives 52a2(Q)=Z/2, and both rational points lie at infinity, so the ordered affine incidence has no Q-point. A nondegenerate point exists over Q(sqrt(53)) at k=2, proving that extension degree two is minimal for an affine point; no constant extension rationalizes the geometrically genus-one family. Over the ordered function field, the two marked invariant sections and two chord-derived anti-invariant sections are independent, with anti-invariant height Gram [[22/3,4/3],[4/3,22/3]] and saturated rank-four MW determinant 13/3. The parameter involution swaps P,Q and T1,T2, so the descended surface over Q(k) has exact arithmetic rank two, not four. Geometrically the K3 has fibres 2IV*+I2+6I1, Picard rank 19, trivial torsion, abs(det NS)=78, and a full integral NS Gram with Smith invariants 1^18,78. The necessary Blichfeldt/Hermite screen for a rootless rank-17 frame passes. No rank-four Q(k) family or actual rootless MW17 fibration is obtained.

entries.scope: For the eleven irreducible squarefree quartics fitted through the published rank-28 fibre at t0=-9529/5471, an exhaustive scan visits all 121589943 primitive rationals t=a/b with |a|<=10000 and 1<=b<=10000. entries.title: High-throughput norm-eight/deep-norm-twelve R17 genus-one splitting search
entries.scope: A diversity-greedy sample of 100 traces from the 1,000 equation-cheapest norm-eight classes and all 43 norm-twelve deep classes gives 143 exact irreducible squarefree branch quartics, each coprime to its trace denominator and the degree-24 R17 surface discriminant. Norm-eight members use distinct generic-section initialization points, no public exceptional targets, and 900 subsequent rational parameter samples from exact group-law multiples on their pointed quartic Jacobians; every norm-twelve deep class has deg(h)=4 and one unique regular quartic member. A dynamic three-word Legendre scanner evaluates 5,474,328 primitive compact or deterministic large-coordinate parameters in twelve primes split into three disjoint blocks, ranks them by weakest-block cover count and F2 trace-mask rank, and leaves 77,704 distinct all-block collisions. Exact testing of every collision performs 160,395 square tests and finds one simultaneous split at t=1/25, for norm-eight class 0x0f6b1 and norm-twelve class 0x103b2. The first point is the neutral generic-section seed. The constructed norm-twelve point is outside the specialized generic MW17 subgroup in independently verified products of E(F_p)/2E(F_p) and E(F_p)/3E(F_p), giving combined finite-quotient rank 18 and an unconditional rank-at-least-18 fibre. The compact height-2000 box is exhaustive, but the trace sample, million-point large-coordinate population, and Jacobian multiple ranges are bounded; local rankings are not Selmer bounds, finite-quotient non-escape is not dependence, and no rank-32 claim is made.

entries.scope: The rational point at t=1/25 points the norm-twelve 0x103b2 genus-one quartic. The interrupted PARI descent supplied no rank upper bound, saturation at 40251553 remains unfinished, and no claim that the 17 points generate all of J(Q), no global pairwise-fibre-product obstruction, and no new K3 specialization-rank claim is made.

entries.title: Minimal elliptic incidence distance two between the two determinant-948 rootless J2 classes
entries.scope: For J2 frame classes on one projective K3, define the one-edge elliptic incidence distance as the minimum F.F' over nef Jacobian fibre classes realizing the two frames. The minimum exists and is symmetric. Distinct J2 classes have distance at least two: intersection zero gives the same primitive fibre ray, while intersection one is carried to the standard U by a fibre-preserving Eichler transvection and therefore has isometric orthogonal complements. For a rootless source NS=U+M(-1), fixed-degree candidates modulo source-section translation are indexed by the finite group M/dM; exact coset minima give the all-section and old-zero costs before the finite horizontal-wall and target-isometry gates. On the pinned determinant-948 H3 surface, all 43 exact norm-twelve genus-one bisections D=(3,2,w) are primitive nef degree-two Jacobian fibre classes sharing the old zero. Exact root enumeration and integral-isometry classification give 33 copies of the published R17 frame and ten copies of the alternate Q80 frame. Hence the two distinct rootless J2 classes have exact incidence distance two, minimum directed zero-section cost one, and a shared-zero witness with relative-U matrix [[2,3],[3,2]] and rank-one bridge Gram [[12,12],[12,12]]. The cheapest stored alternate witness is norm12-orbit-11952. This supersedes the interpretation of the historically transported degree-11511 copy as an intrinsic accessibility obstruction. entries.scope: The universal degree-two compiler applied to every certified norm-twelve shared-zero divisor on the published R17 K3 produces 43 polynomial short Weierstrass models of degrees (8,12,24), with the certified frame distribution 33 published R17 and ten alternate Q80. entries.title: Mass-complete decorated glue calculus for elliptic K3 frame transfer
entries.scope: For two primitive hyperbolic planes in one even lattice, their positive frames share a primitive bridge core K; each frame is a finite graph-glue extension of K plus its orthogonal bridge, and their common roots are exactly the roots of K. The norm-two profile of a class in A_K+A_C is the exact convolution of the low-norm discriminant-coset theta coefficients of K and C. Hence, for a fixed core and bridge universe, root-annihilating mutations are enumerated before child construction by listing isotropic graph subgroups contained in the zero support of that convolution. For good odd-prime neighbours this becomes a split discriminant-plane line swap, with the exact root change determined by the glue-coset root profile. In Picard rank 19, Nikulin uniqueness identifies O(NS)-orbits of primitive U embeddings with rank-17 positive frame classes of the prescribed opposite discriminant form. An exact neighbour BFS whose reciprocal automorphism-order sum closes the genus mass is therefore a terminating decision and construction procedure for rootless MW17 frames at O(NS)/J2 level. The checker validates the local theorem on all 42 marked H3, Q80, NS0024, and Golay-720 corridor edges: every edge is a rank-two cyclic bridge replacement with explicit glue generators and complete removed, surviving, and introduced root sets. This does not give a uniform short-path bound, J1 classification, equation lift, core-generation rule, or speedup theorem.

entries.title: Integral involution eigensublattices and exhaustive E6 graph glue
entries.scope: For an involution of an even lattice, the primitive orthogonal plus and minus eigensublattices have an exponent-two saturation quotient which is exactly the graph of an anti-isometry between 2-elementary discriminant subgroups; conversely every such isotropic graph gives an involution-stable even overlattice. Exhaustive enumeration after the explicit factor-12 integral scaling gives two graph-glue types for E6 2+1, with all three nonzero order-two graphs isometric, and one integral isometry class for all six full F2^2 graph isomorphisms in E6 2+2. entries.title: Local ADE masses as asymptotic Kneser-neighbour root-system frequencies
entries.scope: For any positive even genus G, reciprocal-automorphism root-stratum masses mu_R are determined by the triangular system A_i=sum_R r(R,R_i)mu_R, whose representation totals A_i are Siegel local-density products; in particular mu_0 decides rootless existence and mu_0/mass(G)>=1-a_1/2. For a compact-open marked level K, source x, target spinor genus tau=a*s(x), and good primes with delta_p=a, summing Chenevier's classwise theorem gives N_(p,R)(x)/c_V(p)=mu_R(tau)/(m_K/|S(K)|)+O(p^(-1/2)), improved to O(p^(-1)) above dimension four. Thus for an unmarked one-spinor-genus rank-17 genus the asymptotic root-system frequency is mu_R(G)/mass(G), making mass(G)/mu_R(G) an unguided compatible-line construction score. A fixed compatible prime progression and marked stratum mass are essential when level spinor genera split. The exact calibration emits all 3768 abstract ADE types of rank at most 17 and the 621 types realized by the complete determinant-78 census. Exact primal/dual rational LPs show that every ADE representation row through rank four still allows rootless fraction 11817053639/4286486820968, so it does not force the true census value mu_0=0. All three controls have one proper spinor genus. Determinant 948 has exact rootless mass 3/4 and asymptotic fraction 694167953788108800/77731517730627488307787; four distinct determinant-950 classes give only mu_0>=7/4 and fraction at least 1554936216485363712/152400929187535759901875. No complete integral local-admissibility filter, higher local ADE inversion, exact determinant-950 rootless mass, determinant-948/950 finite-prime frequency, generic composite-determinant class enumerator, equation, or J1 classification is supplied.

entries.title: Retrospective bridge-split root-budget predictor benchmark
entries.scope: On five exact historical H3 first-hit search windows, the mandatory roots in the common rank-15 core plus new rank-two bridge give a safe pre-classification lower bound with no false negatives for the declared target root budgets. entries.title: Exact theta-convolution zero-support glue enumerator
entries.scope: For an even positive split carrier K+C, the norm-two multiplicity in discriminant class (a,b) is the convolution sum_nu theta_K(a,nu)*theta_C(b,2-nu). Therefore an isotropic glue subgroup produces a rootless overlattice exactly when it is contained in the zero support of this convolution. For each of the four terminal H3, Q80, NS0024, and Golay-720 rank-15 cores, the checker starts from the cyclic bridge determinant, independently enumerates every Minkowski-reduced positive even binary bridge, and recovers exactly the fourteen-class bridge universe. It computes and hash-locks every dual-coset theta coefficient through norm two, derives all 28 oriented cyclic graph multipliers from finite-form isotropy alone, and evaluates their convolutions before reading child outcomes or constructing any rank-17 child. It reproduces every independently stored signed child-root count and selects exactly the five rootless bridge classes. This proves an inverse zero-support enumerator on the complete declared fixed-core universe. It does not prove a speedup, generate promising cores automatically, or establish completeness outside those four terminal core/determinant pairs.

entries.title: Maximal-graph core-genus inversion and bounded completion classifier
entries.scope: Let W be the even overlattice of a positive rank-15 core K and positive rank-two bridge C defined by an isotropic graph whose projection to A_C is an isomorphism. The image B in A_K is nondegenerate and anti-isometric to A_C, H-perp/H is B-perp, and therefore q_K is isomorphic to q_W orthogonal-sum (-q_C) with det(K)=det(W)det(C). Conversely, such a finite-form splitting constructs a maximal graph completion with discriminant form q_W. Thus a prescribed Picard-rank-19 frame form q_W=-q_NS and binary bridge C generate the rank-15 core genus before any U, isotropic-divisor, or equation search. For any declared finite bridge universe, the discriminant form decorated by every coset theta coefficient through norm two completely determines the zero-support maximal-graph completion spectrum. The checker verifies the determinant and finite-form identities on both sides of all 42 H3, Q80, NS0024, and Golay-720 clicks, 84 presentations total. At the four positive terminal determinants it independently enumerates 48, 8, 8, and 8 even rank-15 genera and in every case selects a unique genus from q_W orthogonal-sum (-q_C). The four observed core classes have minimum four and their 14 bridge classes contain exactly five zero-support completions. The necessary core-rootlessness gate rejects all 277 primitive cores in the complete held-out E6 source shell before graph enumeration. This is an exact bounded core-first calculus, not an unbounded bridge-determinant cutoff, a uniform or fast rank-15 class enumerator, a complexity or speedup theorem, or an equation-level fibration lift.

entries.title: Reverse theta masks and finite compatible-core signature sieve
entries.scope: For an even positive split carrier K+C and isotropic graph H, define the reverse mask F_(C,H)={(a,2-nu):(a,b) lies in H and theta_C(b,nu)>0}. Nonnegativity of theta convolution proves that the glued lattice is rootless exactly when theta_K vanishes on every cell of F_(C,H). Thus a bridge and graph prescribe the required core vanishings before K is constructed, and only those cells need be queried. If K is rootless of rank r, vectors contributing to one fixed coset theta coefficient through norm two have pairwise nonpositive inner products, so the orthoplex bound gives theta_K(a,nu)<=2r; for rank 15 every nonconstant coefficient lies in {0,...,30}. For a fixed finite quadratic form and declared finite bridge universe, the mask, symmetry and congruence conditions therefore cut out a finite explicitly enumerable outer set of compatible low-order theta signatures. The checker derives all 28 terminal oriented masks, each containing 18--87 cells. Sign symmetry compiles these to exactly 14 unoriented masks of 10--44 cells, and all 14 are minimal under containment. Lazy exact CVP queries reproduce all accept/reject decisions; an independent later full-table phase reproduces all 28 signed root counts, selecting ten orientations or five unoriented bridge classes without constructing a rank-17 child. Across all graphs for the four cores, only 13, 25, 94, and 13 distinct sign-reduced core cells are queried, versus 4418, 8943, 22579, and 5211 occupied cells in the full truth tables. Recorded lazy phases are about 30--85 times faster, but timings are not theorem fields. Direct realization of only lattices having an allowed vector-valued theta signature, a constrained mass formula, an unbounded determinant cutoff, and a uniform speedup theorem remain open.

entries.title: Zero-orbit Weil compression for reverse-theta core generation
entries.scope: In the forced splitting q_K=q_W orthogonal-sum (-q_C), every reverse-theta mask coordinate has A_W-coordinate zero. Averaging a vector-valued theta series over O(q_W) commutes with the Weil representation and preserves those masked Fourier coefficients exactly because zero is a singleton orbit. Modular feasibility may therefore be computed in C[A_W]^{O(q_W)} tensor C[A_C], followed by theta sign symmetry, instead of the full C[A_K]. The checker reconstructs the four terminal q_W and computes orthogonal-invariant dimensions 72, 240, 260, and 240. Including the bridge factor and theta symmetry gives coefficient dimensions 864, 5760, 24960, and 2880 in place of 16560, 44556, 181450, and 21804, exact reductions by factors between 18145/2496 and 115/6. At a good prime splitting each cyclotomic phase field, the exact S,T closure of e_0 has full orbit-quotient dimension in all four cases, so the controls admit no smaller e_0-cyclic reduction. This is an exact compression of the proposed modular prefilter, not an enumeration of compatible modular signatures, realization of a new core lattice, end-to-end core-generation algorithm, or complexity theorem.

entries.title: Compressed modular-dimension audit and linear-mask nonselectivity
entries.scope: For the zero-orbit compressed dual Weil representations attached to the Golay-720, H3, NS0024, and Q80 terminal core genera, the invariant Riemann--Roch trace formula gives exact weight-15/2 modular-form dimensions 476, 3121, 13488, and 1563 and cusp-form dimensions 472, 3120, 13485, and 1562. A reverse mask of m sign-reduced Fourier cells defines at most m linear conditions on the cusp space, so its zero-mask kernel has dimension at least dim(S)-m. Applying this to every one of the fourteen terminal masks gives certified lower bounds from 461 through 13458; in particular every mask leaves a nonzero, highly dimensional cusp kernel. Thus linear modularity plus the reverse vanishings cannot by itself isolate a theta signature or force the modular form to vanish. This does not prove that the affine normalization theta_K(0,0)=1 is feasible for any rejected mask, nor that a surviving modular form has integral nonnegative coefficients or is the theta series of a lattice. Arithmetic theta-cone constraints and lattice realization remain necessary.

entries.title: Bounded mask-aware Kneser generation of a nonhistorical Golay core
entries.scope: For the Golay-720 target frame and the second determinant-23 binary bridge class, the maximal-graph finite-form identity generates a unique even positive rank-15 genus of determinant 16560. Its canonical representative is rootful with 96 signed roots. A deterministic good-prime Kneser beam, seeded by 314159 and scored first by root count and then by occupied reverse-theta mask cells, reaches after seven neighbour steps and 34571 unique raw neighbours a minimum-four rootless core with bridge-class mask profile (3,0). entries.title: Masked-witness survival law and defect-directed Q80 route to the alternate frame
entries.scope: Let K_ell=M_p(K;ell)+Z*y/p be the good-prime Kneser neighbor defined by the isotropic line ell=<y>. For every x in K^dual, x belongs to K_ell^dual if and only if <x,y>=0 modulo p. Hence a line nonorthogonal to every physical dual vector realizing an occupied reverse-mask cell removes the entire old defect, although new forbidden vectors may appear. The exact Q80 near-miss core has two occupied cells realized by four physical witnesses. Of 10000 sampled isotropic lines at 7,11,13,17,19,29,31,37,41,43, exactly 8919 kill all four; 1397 resulting neighbors are rootless, but all acquire replacement defects, with cell-count distribution 2:28, 4:266, 6:584, 8:413, 10:99, 12:7. An isometry-diverse multistep directed beam constructs 30228 distinct neighbors through four generations, including 4643 rootless and 116 with minimal nonzero defect two, before reaching zero support. The four certified transitions remove every parent witness and change physical witness counts 4->6->4->4->0. Appended to the eight-step canonical-seed prefix, they construct a nonhistorical rootless rank-15 core whose class-2 completion has rank 17, determinant 948, minimum four, no roots, 1313 norm-four pairs, and automorphism-group order four. The corridor's historical declared_target_frame is published R17, so its failed isometry test never implied a third class. Combined with the mass-complete determinant-948 J2 classification, the path is a core flow from the Q80 near-miss region around the published target to the other rootless class, alternate Q80. entries.title: Complete good-prime dual-layer defect birth-death law
entries.scope: Let K be a positive-definite even integral lattice, let p be an odd prime not dividing det(K), and let K_ell=M+Z*y/p be the p-neighbor defined by a nonzero isotropic line, with M={z in K:<z,y>=0 mod p} and y^2 divisible by 2p^2. Put K_y^dual={x in K^dual:<x,y>=0 mod p}. Then K_ell^dual is the disjoint union of the p affine layers K_y^dual+j*y/p for 0<=j<p. Under the canonical prime-to-p discriminant identification A_(K_ell)->A_K, the vector x+j*y/p has class [x]. Hence every child theta coefficient through norm two, and in particular every reverse-mask defect, is a finite sum of affine-coset CVP queries. A child has zero defect exactly when the defining line is nonorthogonal to every current physical forbidden witness and no nonzero affine layer contains a forbidden vector. The exact Q80 replay performs the prediction before constructing each child, independently enumerates the materialized child dual afterward, and gets identical physical witness sets and the regression 4->6->4->4->0; the first three births occur only in nonzero layers. The abstract counted signature Sigma_2(K) alone is not sufficient without physical representatives or an equivalent lattice CVP oracle, and no runtime speedup theorem is claimed.

entries.title: Mass-complete finite-prime defect reachability graphs
entries.scope: For the positive even ternary genera of determinants 112, 126, and 316, exact Kneser-neighbor enumeration gives respectively 4, 3, and 9 integral isometry classes, including 1, 1, and 6 rootless zero-support classes; reciprocal automorphism sums equal the exact Minkowski--Siegel masses 3/4, 3/4, and 39/16. For three declared good primes in each genus, every projective isotropic line and child is enumerated, every directed SCC and condensation exit is labelled, every shortest zero path has a prime and isotropic-line witness, and all singleton, pair, and triple prime sets are compared. The determinant-112 directed 3-graph has a closed two-state defective SCC and the determinant-316 directed 3-graph has two closed singleton traps although both unrestricted 3-neighbor graphs are strongly connected. Every two-prime and three-prime union tested has universal zero reachability and maximum distance one. The exact minimum sufficient prime sets are {5},{11} for determinant 112; {5},{11},{13} for determinant 126; and {5},{7} for determinant 316. The determinant-126 directed 5-graph has a shortest defect sequence 2->2->0, so defect count is not distance. All three genera have one proper spinor genus, so fixed-prime traps are not explained by ordinary spinor separation. This is a complete finite root-defect experiment, not a rank-15 marked-mask theorem, an effective all-prime bound, or a universal monotone law.

entries.title: Marked finite-level rootless reachability
entries.scope: Let V be a positive-definite rational quadratic space of dimension greater than two, let Lambda be an integral lattice, and encode a finite discriminant/glue marking by a compact-open level subgroup K^lev of O_V(A_f), with all nonunimodular and marking primes in a finite bad set S. Let X(K^lev) be the finite marked class set, s:X(K^lev)->S(K^lev) its spinor-genus map, and S_1(K^lev) the subgroup of good-prime spinor displacements. Suppose the marking functorially determines a graph-glue completion W_x and its physical reverse-mask witnesses. Then a state x reaches a rootless completion by finitely many witness-killing good-prime core-neighbor edges if and only if a rootless state z exists with s(z)=s(x) modulo S_1(K^lev). In fact, for every sufficiently large good prime p with delta_p=s(z)s(x)^(-1), Chenevier's level-structure equidistribution theorem gives a one-step p-neighbor marked-isomorphic to z. Such a rootless child automatically kills every parent physical witness by the zero-layer survival law and has no replacement birth. The compatible primes form nonempty arithmetic progressions; finiteness of the marked class set gives a finite non-effective sufficient prime set for each component, with at most one prime per required element of S_1(K^lev). Thus fixed-prime traps may persist, but no all-good-prime directed trap exists inside a finite marked component containing a rootless state. No effective prime threshold, infinite-vector marking, core-to-elliptic-neighbor lift, equation, or J1 classification is supplied.
dependencies: external: Chenevier, Statistics for Kneser p-neighbors, Theorem 5.9 and Remarks 5.10--5.11

entries.title: NS0024 completed-core rank-transfer profile
entries.scope: Let S be the determinant-950 Picard-rank-19 Neron--Severi lattice NS0024. Complete the canonical rank-15 core and its exact good-prime Kneser neighbors at p=17,13,7 using the order-191 binary bridge class 4 and the recorded integral graph multipliers. entries.title: Metric physical-witness transfer of the full root system
entries.scope: For an even graph-glue completion W_H of a positive core K and bridge C, the physical norm-two witnesses are exactly the pairs r=k+c in the selected dual cosets with k^2+c^2=2, and their pairwise products are <r,r'>=<k,k'>+<c,c'>. The marking hypothesis is essential: A1^24 and the Niemeier lattice N(24A1) have the same metric root system, while their root primitive-closure quotients are respectively trivial and the binary Golay code (Z/2)^12. entries.title: Target-free projective birth strata for inverse ADE
entries.scope: Let K and C be positive-definite even lattices, H an isotropic graph glue, and p an odd prime coprime to both discriminants. Conversely the norm equation and an adjusted isotropic lift force the affine-kernel orthogonality, so every such scaled-shell vector gives a birth. Hence the no-birth locus is the isotropic projective quadric minus the projective reductions of finitely many scaled dual shells, and the rootless locus additionally removes the hyperplane sections supporting old-root survival. Pairwise products of old and scaled-shell roots give an exact incidence-cell classifier for arbitrary ADE type without a marked target core. An exhaustive checker covers 48 state/prime cases in three mass-closed ternary genera: all 346 predicted physical root sets equal independent materialized-child root sets, and the quadric complements predict exactly all 192 rootless lines. A separate six-line index-two graph-glue control gives 16 nonzero-coset births on every line and again has exact predicted/materialized root-set equality, for 352 comparisons total. entries.title: Specialization quotient, rank-jump sandwich, and midpoint/class-group structure
entries.scope: Let E_eta/K(T) have certified full generic free Mordell--Weil group M_eta of rank r, let E_t/K be a smooth specialization whose image M has rank r, and let M be contained in a certified subgroup L of E_t(K). For every prime ell, the free quotient gain and residual Selmer dimension give rank(L/M) <= rank E_t(K)-r <= dim_Fell(Sel_ell(E_t/K)/bar(M)_ell); without preservation of rank r the left term is only a quotient gain. The canonical-height quotient by M is the orthogonal-complement norm hhat_/M(P)=inf_{u in M tensor R} hhat(P+u), computed by the Schur complement and distinct from an integral coset minimum. For Q in M, orthogonal projection gives hhat(2R-Q)/4=hhat_/M(R mod M)+hhat(pr_M(R)-Q/2), and the paired heights add hhat(R)+hhat(Q-R)=hhat(Q)/2+2hhat_/M(R mod M)+2hhat(pr_M(R)-Q/2). If mu_2(c) is the minimum height in c in M/2M, then the midpoint depth is mu_2(c)/4, the two-torsion-restricted covering radius is max_c sqrt(mu_2(c))/2, and this is a lower bound for the full covering radius. Finally, everywhere-even squareclasses have the ideal square-root map c:ker(v)->Cl(F)[2]. For positive-square-norm subspaces G contained in B supported on S, dim c(ker(v_S|B))/c(ker(v_S|G)) is at least dim(B/G)-(rank v_S(B)-rank v_S(G))-u_F^+; in odd degree u_F^+=r1+r2-1. This last result is a known-point-forced full-class-group image lower bound, not an S-class-group computation, Selmer upper bound, or prospective rank predictor. The theorem package makes no exact specialized-rank or bounded-search claim beyond its stated certified inputs.

entries.title: Global residual Selmer subspaces, Cassels-Tate radical, and covering complexity
entries.scope: For A=E(K), a finitely generated subgroup M of rank r, G=delta(M), and epsilon=dim_F2((A/M)[2]), the Kummer sequence gives W_G=A/(M+2A), an exact sequence 0->W_G->Sel_2/G->Sha[2]->0, and dim W_G=rank(A)-r+epsilon. The residual Cassels-Tate radical modulo W_G is exactly 2 Sha[4], so neither isotropy nor the radical certifies rational solubility. A complete residual pairing of dimension s and rank 2a gives rank(A)<=r+s-2a-epsilon; a partial restricted matrix does not give a full rank bound. For a point P=(a,b) on a short model, the pointed quartic w^2=t^4-6at^2-8bt-3a^2-4A with its explicit birational map phi_P becomes the actual cover delta(P) only with the degree-four map 2phi_P-P. The cubic norm equations give an explicit two-quadric model with rational witness. A generic midpoint centre Q in M has residual cover class zero even though its birational chart discovers points in every W_G class; paired points R and Q-R have the same residual label. Model-and-map encoding cost together with witness cost defines an increasing soluble-class span filtration exhausting W_G, with an exact rank implication and a constructive point-height-to-quartic-coefficient bound. entries.scope: On the short model of the marked rank3 auxiliary Jacobian, the three previously certified independent points and its unique nonzero rational point of order2 have fifteen nonzero parity combinations. Exact duplication-quartic factorization gives no rational half for any combination. A separate Sage-free verifier multiplies every factorization, checks a finite-prime no-root certificate for every nonlinear factor, performs exact rational-square tests and replays group doubling on all rational lifts. The2-torsion cubic is classified by the same independent method. Thus the subgroup is2-saturated. No original-fibre point search, new specialized rank, full integral Mordell-Weil basis or full-carrier parameter-height bound follows.
